solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Continues the book, dismissing detective’s first motive (6)

indicatorNotes.dismissing: to dismiss someone is to send them out of the room, so D is sent out of READS ON

blocks.note: to read on is to continue a book
first letter of detective, taken out of READS ON

annotation.surface: A reader keeps going with a whodunnit, still hunting for the killer's motive.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive and 'first' look like part of a crime-fiction sentence; together they only pick out the D to be removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the reason behind an act is its motive.

entries.clue: Ecstatic, intoxicated rich hosts upset party resort (9)

indicatorNotes.intoxicated: a drunk person cannot keep things in order, so the letters of RICH stagger into a new arrangement
indicatorNotes.hosts: a host has guests inside the house, so RHIC holds the other letters within it
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, to upset something is to tip it over, so its letters read from the bottom up

annotation.surface: A wealthy, drunken host is thrilled to throw a party at a resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' covers both the party and the resort, not just the party, and in a down entry the tipped-over pair reads upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to be rhapsodic is to be carried away with enthusiasm, ecstatic.

entries.clue: Very good set in a French city? Mostly (7)

indicatorNotes.set in: to set something in a frame is to place it inside, so GEL is placed inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.Mostly: most but not all of the word is used, so NICE is cut before its final E

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a very fine place is a French city, half-sure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' does two jobs: it is the word for GEL, and 'set in' says where GEL goes.
annotation.definitionFit: By extension: angels are the model of goodness, so an angelic child is very good.

entries.clue: Doctor Who is left looking wise (6)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it, as with doctored figures, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: The Doctor from Doctor Who is left looking thoughtful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' is the famous BBC time-traveller, so the eye reads it as a name; here 'Doctor' is a verb acting on 'Who is' plus L.
annotation.definitionFit: The owl is the proverbial wise bird, so to look owlish is to look wise.

entries.clue: Rabbit initially confused with Wonderland character (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the start of 'confused' is taken

blocks.note: the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland

annotation.surface: The White Rabbit is getting muddled up with another Alice in Wonderland character.
annotation.walkthrough: Wonderland really has a White Rabbit, which is why the first word looks like a character too.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: to rabbit (on) is to talk at length, to chatter.

entries.clue: Philanthropy must do without it, displaying caution (5)

indicatorNotes.must do without: to do without something is to go on having lost it, so CHARITY carries on minus IT

blocks.note: the word itself, removed from CHARITY

annotation.surface: A cautious remark that philanthropy will have to manage without some funding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun for the missing money; it is the literal letters to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: chary means wary, reluctant to take risks.

entries.clue: Letters help to support Vaughan Williams, say, after overture lost (8)

indicatorNotes.overture lost: an overture is the opening of a piece, so losing it means the first letter goes
indicatorNotes.to support: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so ABET goes below, after ALPH

blocks.note: RALPH Vaughan Williams, the English composer, minus his first letter

annotation.surface: A letter writer offers help to the composer Vaughan Williams after one of his overtures went missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Vaughan Williams as an example of a Ralph. Overture sounds musical, fitting the composer, but only means the R.
annotation.definitionFit: Collective sense: the alphabet is the full set of letters.

entries.clue: Children’s game and story incorporating new slogan (7)

indicatorNotes.incorporating: to incorporate is to take into the body, so LIE takes N into its middle

blocks.note: a story is a fib, a lie

annotation.surface: A children's game and a story come bundled with a fresh advertising slogan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Story' sounds like a bedtime tale to go with the game; it is the fib sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a tagline is a catchphrase attached to a brand or film.

entries.clue: Rhubarb that chap dipped in drink (5)

indicatorNotes.dipped in: something dipped in a drink ends up inside it, so HE goes inside RUM

blocks.note: rum is a drink, the outer piece

annotation.surface: A stick of rhubarb that some fellow has dunked in his drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Most solvers know rheum only as the watery discharge from eyes; the botanical name is the less familiar sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Botanical name: Rheum is the genus to which rhubarb belongs.

entries.clue: Incumbent to be not entirely long (8)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: not entirely means not the whole thing, so OCCUR is given without its end

blocks.note: to occur is to be (found), as in 'the word occurs twice'; minus R
to long for is to pant for

annotation.surface: An office-holder-in-waiting whose term turns out to be not quite long.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Incumbent to be' reads as 'incumbent-elect'; in fact 'to be' is its own piece, OCCUR.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the incumbent of a post is the one currently holding, or occupying, it.

entries.clue: Everybody welcoming energy in star (5)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: to welcome guests is to take them in, so ALL takes GO inside

annotation.surface: Everyone is making a star feel welcome and energetic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity being welcomed; it is a real star in the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: Proper name: Algol is a bright variable star in Perseus, the 'demon star'.

entries.clue: Winner with time to swallow new celebratory drink? (9)

indicatorNotes.to swallow: what is swallowed ends up inside, so AGE takes N into it

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A winner takes time to gulp down a fresh drink to celebrate.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes the podium ritual, so the definition sits inside its own scene.
annotation.definitionFit: By association: champagne is the drink traditionally opened to celebrate.

entries.clue: Speak about Irish city, but not northern city (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about means surrounding, so SAY goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.not northern: N stands for northern, so 'not northern' strikes an N out

blocks.note: to say is to speak, the outer piece
LISBURN, a city in Northern Ireland, minus N

annotation.surface: Someone talks about an Irish city but insists it is not a northern one.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that Lisburn is in Northern Ireland; 'not northern' only drops its final N. Salisbury is a cathedral city in Wiltshire, England.
annotation.definitionFit: Proper name: Salisbury is an English cathedral city.

entries.clue: Universal principle? Nothing in principle abandoned by leader (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in says where O goes: inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.abandoned by leader: a word abandoned by its leader has lost its first letter, so MAXIM drops the M

blocks.note: a maxim is a principle; minus M

annotation.surface: A universal principle is questioned: a party leader has given up on principle entirely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Principle' is written twice, once in the definition and once as MAXIM. 'Leader' reads as a politician; it is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an axiom is a principle accepted as universally true.

entries.clue: Wharf where criminals are often seen? (4)

blocks.note: first definition: a berth where ships load and unload
second definition: the enclosure in a courtroom where the accused stands

annotation.surface: A quay where villains are often spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: The docks sound like a crooks' hangout; the second sense is the dock in a courtroom, where the accused stands.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a dock is a wharf for ships, and the courtroom dock is the enclosure for the accused.

entries.clue: Chap leading representative to secure me for the board? (10)

indicatorNotes.leading: whoever leads goes in front, so MAN comes first
indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure something is to hold it fast, so AGENT holds ME inside

annotation.surface: A man heading an agency hopes to get me appointed to the board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Secure me for the board' reads as a job appointment; 'secure' is the container, and 'for' links to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Collective sense: a company's board is its management.

entries.clue: Comment on article, no thanks to editor first and foremost (8)

indicatorNotes.first and foremost: foremost means at the very front, so only the front letter of each word counts

blocks.note: first letters of to and editor

annotation.surface: A remark about an article, with no gratitude shown to the editor above all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is everyday British for thank you. 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece to comment on; it is just AN.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to annotate a text is to add comments to it.

entries.clue: Drunk grabbing a harmful bit of car (4-5)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: to grab is to seize and hold, so TIGHT holds the other letters inside

annotation.surface: A drunk is snatching a dangerous part off a car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' leads the clue like a noun, the person doing the grabbing; it is the adjective TIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Part for whole: a tail-light is the red lamp on the back of a car.

entries.clue: Reduction in wharf rail transport — just a few lines here (8)

indicatorNotes.Reduction in: a reduction makes something smaller, so QUAY is cut short by its last letter

annotation.surface: Cuts to trains serving the wharf leave only a few railway lines there.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'lines' look like railway track; they are lines of verse.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: a quatrain is a stanza of only four lines of verse.

entries.clue: Advisor working with sovereign in court (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces are in court, and court is CT, so they sit inside C…T

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court, the outer piece
a machine that is on is working
a sultan is a sovereign ruler

annotation.surface: An advisor works alongside the monarch at the royal court.
annotation.walkthrough: The royal court fits the sovereign so well that 'court' reads as the scene rather than the abbreviation CT.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a consultant is a paid professional advisor.

entries.clue: Subtle nude dancing around party in Pretoria (7)

indicatorNotes.dancing: letters that dance move about, so NUDE is rearranged
indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go either side of ANC

blocks.note: the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

annotation.surface: A discreet nude dance performed at a party in the South African capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Pretoria' just locates the party in South Africa; ANC is fixed in the middle while only NUDE moves.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something nuanced shows fine shades of meaning, so it is subtle.

entries.clue: Satirical writer approves a Kindle’s content (4)

indicatorNotes.content: the content of something is what it holds inside, so the answer lies within the words

annotation.surface: A satirist gives his blessing to the reading matter on a Kindle.
annotation.walkthrough: Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, writer of sharp satirical short stories. 'Content' looks like the Kindle's reading matter.
annotation.definitionFit: Pen name: Saki (H. H. Munro) was an Edwardian writer of satirical short stories.

entries.clue: Complain about island accommodating heads of insurgent group (7)

indicatorNotes.accommodating: to accommodate guests is to house them, so ARRAN houses IG
indicatorNotes.heads of: the head of a word is its first letter, so insurgent and group each give their first

blocks.note: Arran, an island off the west of Scotland, the outer piece
first letters of insurgent and group

annotation.surface: Complaints about an island that is sheltering rebel leaders.
annotation.walkthrough: The rebel group sounds like the target of the complaint, but it only supplies two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Formal sense: to arraign someone is to find fault with or accuse them.

entries.clue: Paltry, exhibiting paltriness reduced by cunning (6)

indicatorNotes.reduced: something reduced is made shorter, so MEAN loses its last letter

annotation.surface: Something paltry, made even more so by crafty trimming.
annotation.walkthrough: Mean here is the stingy sense, and 'paltriness' echoes the definition on purpose.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: measly means contemptibly small, as in a measly tip.

entries.clue: A lot of rubbish covering large item in garden (5)

indicatorNotes.A lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so PANTS loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over and around, so PANT wraps around L

blocks.note: PANTS, British slang for rubbish, minus S
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A heap of rubbish is covering something big in the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means rubbish or nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a plant is the typical thing growing in a garden.

entries.clue: Italian food not to be found at the start of the dictionary? (5)

blocks.clueFragment: not to be found at the start
blocks.note: beyond the start of the dictionary
A is the letter a dictionary begins with

annotation.surface: A remark that the Italian word for this food is not listed at the front of the dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: A word found after the A section is 'past A', which spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Category: pasta is the family of Italian dough foods, spaghetti and the rest.

entries.clue: Church guy and doctor make better nurses (9)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse a baby is to hold it close, so HEAL holds DR inside

blocks.note: to heal is to make better, the outer piece

annotation.surface: A churchman and a doctor improve the lot of nurses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' reads as the hospital staff that a doctor works with; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Hypernym: a cathedral is a bishop's principal church.

entries.clue: Gang almost securing one million in heist? (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means nearly all, so CREW stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.securing: to secure loot is to hold on to it, so CRE holds I and M inside

annotation.definitionNote: the question mark marks a heist as one example of a crime
annotation.surface: A gang nearly bags a million in a robbery.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as the heist itself; the question mark shows a heist is just one kind of crime.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a heist, a big robbery, is one kind of crime.

entries.clue: Left-winger very much linked to US spy records? (9)

blocks.note: so = very much, as in 'so kind'

annotation.surface: A left-winger strongly tied to American intelligence files.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a leftist on the CIA's books is an unlikely picture; 'records' is a verb, LIST, not files.
annotation.definitionFit: Political sense: socialists sit on the left wing of politics.

entries.clue: Perform like Ella Fitzgerald, enshrining women’s jazz (5)

indicatorNotes.enshrining: to enshrine a relic is to enclose it in a shrine, so SING encloses W

blocks.note: Ella Fitzgerald was a famous singer, the outer piece

annotation.surface: Singing in Ella Fitzgerald's style, keeping women's jazz alive.
annotation.walkthrough: Ella Fitzgerald sang swing, so the answer is right there in the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyponym: swing is a style of big-band jazz.

entries.clue: Piece of music with an opening for the flute at last (7)

indicatorNotes.an opening for: the opening of a word is where it starts, so 'the' gives its first letter
indicatorNotes.at last: at last means at the very end, so 'flute' gives only its final letter

annotation.surface: A composition that finally gives the flute a chance to play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An opening for the flute' reads as a solo cue; 'an' is its own piece and 'the' is the word whose opening is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Tempo term: an andante is a movement or piece played at a walking pace.

entries.clue: Small bird, clearly grown and elegant, looking at the wings (6)

indicatorNotes.looking at the wings: the wings of a stage are its two sides, so each word gives its two ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of clearly
first and last letters of grown
first and last letters of elegant

annotation.surface: A little bird, plainly grown and graceful, inspecting its wings.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the ugly duckling becoming a swan; 'wings' is the outer letters of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a cygnet is a young swan, a bird not yet full size.
